messages:
eli: Heads up — smallbatch perf regression on main after the driver + torch bump merged last night. 90th latency up ~35% on seq<=64 flows. CI perf alerted. <https://ci.redwood.local/job/perf-smallbatch/234>
maya: saw it too, reproduces locally on a100 with cuda 12.6.3 + pytorch 2.3.1. pprof shows a different matmul/epilogue kernel chosen for tiny batches.
kevin: interesting — autotune table is picking a different kernel id for batch=4, seq=32. attached cheap flame from a failing run.
eli: pasted flame snippet into thread:
```
# hot path
matmul_kernel_v3  48.2%
matmul_kernel_v1  12.7%
kv_cache_prefetch 9.1%
other 29.9%
```
maya: kernel_v3 is the new triton-generated path (post-driver changes). latency for that kernel is worse at small tile sizes.
infra-ci: perf job failed: https://ci.redwood.local/job/perf-smallbatch/234 (regression +22% tokens/s). artifacts: profile.tar.gz
kevin: quick local test: toggling TRITON_AUTO_TUNE=0 forces old kernel path and restores baseline numbers. can someone run the smoke harness with that env set in CI?
eli: started a gated run: `./scripts/run_perf.sh --suite smallbatch --env TRITON_AUTO_TUNE=0` — restoring perf locally.
maya: probable root cause = autotune heuristics + slight cuBLAS/cuTENSOR dispatch change in 12.6.3. kernel selection heuristic now prefers a tile that triggers less favorable register spilling on a100 for short sequences.
sre-ops: rolling this up — create revert PR for the merge that bumped pytorch/driver? or pin triton/autotune to previous heuristic. Which is lower risk for rollout?
kevin: quick options: 1) set TRITON_AUTO_TUNE=0 in rollout (fast) 2) revert merge (safer long-term but noisy) 3) opcode-level patch to selection heuristic (needs testing).
eli: i'm creating a temporary hotfix: config change + canary to dedicated region. PR link once ready.
deploy-bot: nightly-canary deployment queued: https://deploy.redwood.local/deploy/6789 — will include env override TRITON_AUTO_TUNE=0
maya: also adding a regression test to perf harness to catch kernel-id shifts for seq<=64 so CI will fail next time.
kevin: planning a bisect over the triton/autotune commits from the last two weeks if config flip doesn't fully resolve. will report back with the culprits.
eli: thanks. tagging @sre-ops for rollback authority if canary shows no perf win. :thumbsup:
sre-ops: acknowledged — ready to rollback if canary doesn't improve within the hour.
